name: CA-27
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+6 partisan lean and Democratic incumbent advantage
Whitesides' overwhelming financial edge: $3.96M raised and $2.55M on hand versus $379K and $202K for Gibbs
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 93% to win
No public general-election polling, leaving the forecast dependent on fundamentals
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to the incumbent: a D+6 district, a two-point incumbency bonus, and a lopsided money advantage of roughly ten-to-one in receipts. Markets agree, pricing Whitesides around 93%, so a modest trim from the baseline still leaves the Democrat a heavy favorite.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Whitesides under 55%, or significant outside spending entering for Gibbs, would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent George T. Whitesides (D) is running.

overview:
First-term incumbent George Whitesides defends a northern Los Angeles County seat that leans Democratic by about six points. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised nearly $4 million and holding $2.55 million on hand, while Republican Jason Gibbs has raised under $400,000 with about $200,000 available. Outside spending has been minimal and one-sided so far.

With no public general-election polls available, the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency edge, and the fundraising gap, all of which favor the Democrat. Prediction markets likewise price Whitesides as a heavy favorite. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of polling, which keeps the error band wider than in a well-surveyed race.
